rationale.complete: Round 1 done: pre-registered predictions, synthetic validation (finite-N branching and the full pipeline on real village timelines), 32 per-period verdicts, cross-period tests, a scorecard, and a frozen, dry-run confirmatory script (not run). No natural-experiment test or holdout run yet. Round 1b (2026-10-04): re-run on context-ledger visibility with an H57 read-vs-unread placebo, and two ground-truth natives (#35 lead designers, #26 elected leader).
rationale.faithfulness: The subcritical, exposure-driven branching description holds everywhere (32/32 subcritical; HR10 beats the validated field null in 27/32), so C, D, F, G, H and I are each 1. The literal claim (a power law whose exponent reads criticality, tied to activity loop gains) failed. There is no s^-3/2, tau_app is just R-hat, P4 gave rho = 0.06, tails are heavier than one branching law, and the pre-registered forecast was overconfident. E = 0. Round 1b: HR10 now passes 32/32 (regime I was mismeasured), but not-yet-read uses predict adoption at about half the strength of read ones, so part of the exposure lock is convergence; known leaders are not idea sources. Axes unchanged.
rationale.usefulness: A computable rule: R-hat from two days of logs gives next-day reach probabilities for new ideas or claims, and the post-hoc version is roughly calibrated (70-84% at 90%). The practical negative results also help: activity gains don't proxy idea spread, and exposure ordering can't separate copying from independent invention in a shared room. The calibration evidence is post hoc and the rule is unconfirmed, hence between a diagnostic (2) and a validated monitor (3).

one_line: Idea cascades are strongly subcritical (R about 0.2) and heavy-tailed, not power-law; about half the exposure lock is convergence, not copying.
